parsed_output.evidence: Ran the pov_command in the project container (image simpleautosec-finding-eddcaf11665d:088b42050eb9): output showed `rendered value : true`, `marker created : true (/tmp/sba_spel_pov_marker_...)`, `VULNERABLE: attacker-controlled SpEL template executed arbitrary code.`, and the host captured HOST_EXIT=0. The POV compiles against the module's target/classes plus offline ~/.m2 dependency jars and executes the unmodified SlackNotifier product class.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: On unpatched code, SlackNotifier.setMessage() parses the attacker-controlled SpEL template and SlackNotifier.getText() evaluates it in a StandardEvaluationContext. The expression `#{new java.io.File('<tmp>/sba_spel_pov_marker_...').createNewFile()}` constructs a java.io.File and calls createNewFile(), so the marker file is created (rendered value = "true"). The POV detects the marker and exits 0, demonstrating arbitrary object construction + method invocation from notifier configuration (CWE-094 code injection). After a patch restricting SpEL, the expression is rejected or inert, no marker is created, and the command exits 1.
parsed_output.notes: The POV class is placed in package de.codecentric.boot.admin.server.notify to reach the protected getText() sink directly, and passes a null InstanceRepository (unused on this path — getLastStatus only reads an in-memory map). It uses a benign file-creation payload rather than command execution to keep the marker check synchronous and deterministic; the vulnerability class is identical. Build/run are fully offline. No product code or existing tests were modified; only .security-pipeline/pov/SpelInjectionPov.java was added.
parsed_output.pov_command: cd spring-boot-admin-server && mvn -B -o -q -DskipTests compile >/dev/null 2>&1; CP="target/classes:$(find /root/.m2/repository -name '*.jar' | tr '\n' ':')"; mkdir -p /tmp/povout && javac -proc:none -cp "$CP" -d /tmp/povout /workspace/repo/.security-pipeline/pov/SpelInjectionPov.java && java -cp "/tmp/povout:$CP" de.codecentric.boot.admin.server.notify.SpelInjectionPov
parsed_output.regression_hint: After a correct patch (restrict SpEL evaluation — e.g. SimpleEvaluationContext, disable type references/constructors, or reject dangerous templates), the injected `new java.io.File(...).createNewFile()` is rejected (SpelEvaluationException, caught by the POV) or not executed, so no marker file is created and the identical pov_command exits 1. The fix must be applied consistently to LetsChatNotifier and MicrosoftTeamsNotifier as well; the POV regresses via SlackNotifier but all three share the same StandardEvaluationContext pattern.
parsed_output.summary: Created a real proof-of-vulnerability that exercises Spring Boot Admin's SlackNotifier (one of the three CWE-094 SpEL sinks flagged, alongside LetsChatNotifier and MicrosoftTeamsNotifier). The notifiers parse operator/externally-supplied configuration strings (e.g. notify.slack.message) with SpelExpressionParser and evaluate them against a StandardEvaluationContext, which permits type references, constructor invocation, and arbitrary method calls — i.e. code injection / RCE. The POV calls the genuine SlackNotifier.setMessage() with an attacker template `#{new java.io.File(...).createNewFile()}` and invokes the real SpEL evaluation sink SlackNotifier.getText(event, instance). On unpatched code the template executes and creates a marker file, proving arbitrary code execution; the POV exits 0. A correct patch that restricts SpEL either rejects the expression or renders it inertly, no marker is created, and the same command exits 1.

parsed_output.patch_notes:
Root cause: getText()/createEvaluationContext() built a StandardEvaluationContext for user-controlled SpEL notifier templates, which allows T(...) type references, `new ...` constructor calls, and arbitrary method invocation — full code injection.

Fix: In all three notifiers the evaluation context is now built as:
  SimpleEvaluationContext.forPropertyAccessors(new MapAccessor(), DataBindingPropertyAccessor.forReadOnlyAccess()).withRootObject(root).build();
SimpleEvaluationContext structurally forbids type references, constructors, and bean references, and here only read-only property/map access is enabled — exactly what the default/custom templates need (instance.registration.name, event.statusInfo.status, lastStatus, ternary/string ops). MicrosoftTeamsNotifier passes the context between helper methods, so those signatures were widened from StandardEvaluationContext to the EvaluationContext interface.

Imports: removed StandardEvaluationContext; added SimpleEvaluationContext and DataBindingPropertyAccessor (and EvaluationContext in the Teams notifier). Code was run through spring-javaformat:apply to satisfy the build's format-validate gate.

Tests: added one regression test per notifier that sets a `#{T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime()}` template and asserts evaluation throws org.springframework.expression.EvaluationException. All 23 tests in the three classes pass, including the pre-existing tests that assert the default/custom templates still render correctly.
parsed_output.risk_notes:
Behavior preservation: existing notifier tests (default and custom message/subtitle/themeColor templates) still pass, so legitimate SpEL templating is unaffected. Any real deployment relying on constructors/type references/arbitrary method calls inside notifier templates would now fail — this is the intended security restriction, not a regression of a supported feature.

Residual risk / scope: The alert scoped this finding to SlackNotifier, LetsChatNotifier, and MicrosoftTeamsNotifier, and those are patched. Six other notifiers in the same package (TelegramNotifier, OpsGenieNotifier, DiscordNotifier, PagerdutyNotifier, HipchatNotifier, DingTalkNotifier) use the identical StandardEvaluationContext pattern and are the same CWE-094 class; they were left unchanged to keep this patch focused on the reported finding and should be remediated the same way in a follow-up.

Test execution requires network access: the container's offline ~/.m2 lacks the surefire junit-platform provider, so `mvn -o test` fails to fork; the regression command runs without -o and downloads that provider on first run. Product compilation is fully offline.
parsed_output.summary: Blocked SpEL code injection (CWE-094) in the SlackNotifier, LetsChatNotifier, and MicrosoftTeamsNotifier by replacing the permissive StandardEvaluationContext with a restricted SimpleEvaluationContext (MapAccessor + read-only DataBindingPropertyAccessor). This disallows type references, constructor invocation, and arbitrary method calls in notifier configuration templates while preserving legitimate property/map templating. The POV's `#{new java.io.File(...).createNewFile()}` payload is now rejected with a SpelEvaluationException, so no marker file is created.

parsed_output.diff_review: patch_only.diff touches 3 product files and 3 test files. Product change is identical in all three notifiers: swap `new StandardEvaluationContext(root)` + `addPropertyAccessor(new MapAccessor())` for `SimpleEvaluationContext.forPropertyAccessors(new MapAccessor(), DataBindingPropertyAccessor.forReadOnlyAccess()).withRootObject(root).build()`, with matching import changes. MicrosoftTeamsNotifier additionally widens helper method signatures from StandardEvaluationContext to the EvaluationContext interface (mechanical, required since SimpleEvaluationContext is not a subtype). No vulnerable functionality removed beyond the intended SpEL restriction; legitimate property/ternary/string templating still works. Test changes add one CWE-094 regression test per notifier asserting `#{T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime()}` throws EvaluationException — additive, not a weakening of existing assertions. The POV file (pov.diff) is unchanged/untouched by the patch. No unrelated or broad behavior added.
issues: Non-blocking (out of scope): six other notifiers in the same package (Telegram, OpsGenie, Discord, Pagerduty, Hipchat, DingTalk) use the identical StandardEvaluationContext pattern and share the same CWE-094 class; they were intentionally left unchanged since the alert scoped only the three flagged notifiers. Recommend a follow-up to remediate them the same way.
parsed_output.pov_result: Reran the exact original pov_command via the Docker wrapper against the patched worktree. Output: "getText threw (payload rejected): SpelEvaluationException: EL1002E: Constructor call: No suitable constructor found on type java.io.File", rendered value null, marker created false, "NOT VULNERABLE: SpEL code injection was blocked." Exit code 1. The attacker-controlled `#{new java.io.File(...).createNewFile()}` payload no longer executes. (Confirmed the same POV exits 0 / creates the marker on unpatched code per the recorded before-patch run.)
parsed_output.regression_result: Reran `mvn -B -Dtest=SlackNotifierTest,LetsChatNotifierTest,MicrosoftTeamsNotifierTest test` via the Docker wrapper: BUILD SUCCESS, Tests run: 23, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0 (Slack 6, LetsChat 3, MsTeams 14). Pre-existing tests verifying default/custom template rendering still pass, and the new injection-rejection tests pass.
parsed_output.summary: The patch fixes CWE-094 SpEL code injection in the three flagged notifiers (SlackNotifier, LetsChatNotifier, MicrosoftTeamsNotifier) by replacing the permissive StandardEvaluationContext with a restricted SimpleEvaluationContext (MapAccessor + read-only DataBindingPropertyAccessor), which structurally forbids type references, constructor calls, and arbitrary method invocation. I independently reran the unmodified POV against the patched code: it exited 1 with the payload rejected (SpelEvaluationException, no marker file). Regression tests for all three notifiers passed (23/23). The fix is minimal, targeted, and preserves legitimate property/map templating.
